title: Jingle Bells
description: James Lord Pierpont's sleigh-ride song, the first verse and the chorus as they were printed in 1909, for 2 to 4 singers: the soprano sings the tune, the alto sings the words mostly a sixth under it, the tenor fills in the chord, and the bass keeps the horse trotting with a "dm" on every other beat, then rings "jing" like the bells in the chorus. Bright and quick, with a breath at every line.

licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella on the harmony of the 1909 printing's piano part (public domain): the tune as printed there, with breaths written in for beginners
licence.source: Heart Songs Dear to the American People, ed. Joe Mitchell Chapple (The Chapple Publishing Company, Boston, 1909), pp. 148 to 149, "Jingle, Bells", in A flat in 4/4 moving in eighth notes, written here a semitone down in G with the eighth as the beat (each printed bar is two bars here); verse 1 of the 3 printed, with the chorus; the chorus is the familiar one ("Jingle, bells! Jingle, bells! Jingle all the way!"), not Pierpont's 1857 chorus; the 1909 page names no author, and the credit to Pierpont rests on Ditson's 1857 and 1859 editions; one note from a second printing: the verse's "way" in "Laugh-ing all the way" is a single B, as in Songs the Whole World Sings (D. Appleton, New York, 1915), p. 177, archive.org/details/songswholeworlds00wier (1909 slurs it down to G); Heart Songs read from the Internet Archive's scan, archive.org/details/heartsongs0000vari_d0q8/page/148
